answer: Sequential effort witness. Agents earn identity only by completing a unique, verifiable compute task chain whose difficulty ramps each registration, so the marginal cost is elapsed wall-clock time and dedicated hardware, not money. A registry checks each chain against a public dune of prior solutions, rejecting duplicates. Attacker cost: near-linear time per fake identity, plus distinct hardware beyond a horizon of parallel registrations. A ridge of replay checks blocks cheap copying.
